newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland guarantees loans for Warsaw wholesale market.
newsitem.headline: Poland guarantees loans for Warsaw wholesale market.

text.p: The government guaranteed a $15 million loan by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and a $10 million loan by Kredyt Bank SA for the construction of a wholesale market near Warsaw.

The guarantees, approved on Tuesday, cleared the way for the construction of the Warsaw Food and Agriculture Wholesale Market SA (WRSRH), which is to be completed by the end of 1998, a market official said.
"We can start building even tomorrow now that we can sign credit agreements (with these banks)," Janusz Lucki, financial director at WRSRH told reporters befor the signing ceremony.
Lucki said that the agreements with the EBRD and Kredyt Bank would secure two-thirds of the 160 million zlotys needed for the construction of the market.
WRSRH had already raised 35 million zlotys through share issues and there would be at least three more new share issues directed to future market participants.
The wholesale market, based on a concept developed through the European Union's (EU) PHARE programme, plans to have daily turnover of about $1 million, Lucki said.
Hans Jacobsen, a director of EBRD's agriculture team, also present, said WRSRH, which will trade only foodstuffs and flowers, will give farmers a steady market for their goods.
